# Time Series Forecasting

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **In practice** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-time-series-forecasting/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-time-series-forecasting/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

How to forecast demand a day ahead and check that the forecast holds up: baselines, backtests that never see the future, statistical models, one LightGBM model for all clients, totals that add up, and calibrated prediction intervals, on hourly electricity demand from thirty clients.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

For data scientists and analysts who know pandas and basic regression and are asked to forecast demand, such as sales, energy, tickets or traffic, and need forecasts that hold up when they are checked.

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.13.16
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python load-lead-client.py
```

Model outputs are recorded once in `examples/data/recorded/`, each folder with a `manifest.json` that names the model, its exact version and the script that recorded it, so the examples never call a model. `recordings/` holds the scripts that record them again.

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, every example runs again in the new version. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/time-series-forecasting/changes).
